summary: A 1921 'rag outfit' lookout on the Cabinet Ranger District, rebuilt in 1939 and again in 1964, staffed into the 1970s and now a recreation.gov rental.

facts.design: R-6 flattop cab with catwalk on a 30-foot treated timber tower

access.note: Overnight stays by reservation on recreation.gov; check the listing for road, trail and seasonal closures.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Kootenai National Forest, Cabinet Ranger District

events.note: Activated as a 'rag outfit': a pole platform tent near an open platform tower
L-4 cab built on a 20-foot pole tower
Current R-6 flattop cab with catwalk built on a 30-foot timber tower
Registered August 20, 1996 as US 180 / MT 19, nominated by Gary Weber, FFLA

evidence.supports: location: Kootenai National Forest, Sanders County
evidence.quote:
Kootenai National Forest
Sanders County, Montana

Gem Peak Lookout was activated in 1921 as a U.S. Forest Service “rag outfit” -- a pole platform tent near an open platform tower and remained that way nearly two decades until an L-4 on a 20 pole tower was built in 1939. In 1964 the present R-6 Flattop cab with catwalk on 30 timber tower was constructed and staffed through the 1970s.

evidence.supports: one of three rental lookouts on the Cabinet Ranger District
evidence.quote: It is now one of three rental lookouts on the Cabinet Ranger District.

evidence.supports: registered August 20, 1996, nominated by Gary Weber, FFLA, as US 180 / MT 19

evidence.supports: 15-foot pole platform tower, no permanent quarters until 1939
evidence.quote: Started as a camp lookout with a 15' pole platform tower, Gem Peak remained the only one of the Noxon Ranger District's regular lookouts without permanent living quarters until 1939 when a 20' pole tower with L-4 cab was built.

evidence.supports: 1964 30-foot timber tower with R-6 flat cab, staffed into the 1970s
evidence.quote: In 1964, the present 30' treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab was constructed. Staffed into the 1970's, it is now on the Recreation Rental program, and is listed on the National Historic Lookout Register.

evidence.supports: named lookout personnel: Vic Six 1959, Jan Fisher 1961-1962, Gary Meyer 1967
evidence.quote: Known lookout personnel: 1959: Vic Six; 1961-1962: Jan Fisher; 1967: Gary Meyer.

corrections.why: Both sources describe the current (1964) structure as a 30-foot timber tower; 6.1 m (~20 ft) matches the 1939 L-4 tower height, not the current one.

notes_for_editor: Two independent, detailed sources agree closely on the build history (1921 rag outfit -> 1939 L-4 on 20-ft pole tower -> 1964 R-6 flattop on 30-ft timber tower) and on staffing into the 1970s. Flagged a likely height_m error in the tower record (20 ft vs. the current 30-ft tower). Minor elevation discrepancy not flagged: NHLR gives 6,029 ft (1,838 m, matches record); firelookout.com gives 6,092 ft -- not material enough for a correction. Did not need to use the web-search budget; both cached pages were sufficient. Fact-check 2026-10-04: removed an uncited 'Clark Fork River country' detail from the opening sentence (not in either source) and rewrote two sentences that too closely copied source wording ('rag outfit' tent description; 'without permanent living quarters' line). Spot-checked the NHLR registry-number/date quote and both firelookout.com quotes (location and named personnel) directly against fetch_text.py output; all three matched the source exactly.
